questions.question: Which Consul component participates in the Raft voting peer set?
options: Every application process
Server agents only
Client agents only
Every Envoy sidecar
questions.explanation: Only Consul server agents form the Raft peer set and vote on replicated state. Client agents run near workloads, perform local checks, and forward control-plane requests.

questions.question: What is the main difference between gossip membership and Raft consensus?
options: Gossip detects membership and broadcasts events; Raft orders and commits authoritative control-plane state
Gossip stores ACL tokens; Raft performs DNS recursion
Gossip encrypts service traffic; Raft replaces sidecar proxies
There is no operational difference
questions.explanation: LAN and WAN gossip spread membership and failure information. Raft runs among server agents and requires a quorum to commit catalog, ACL, configuration, and other authoritative state.

questions.question: A service accepts TCP connections but its request handler is deadlocked. Which check is most likely to keep the unsafe instance marked passing?
options: An HTTP readiness check that exercises the handler
A TCP port check
A TTL check owned by the request loop
A gRPC health check implemented by the service
questions.explanation: A TCP check proves only that a connection can be established. It does not prove the application can complete useful work, so its contract can be too shallow for readiness.

questions.question: Why can Consul DNS still return a result when the server cluster has no leader?
options: DNS silently creates a new Raft cluster
DNS uses stale reads by default, so a reachable follower can answer from replicated state
DNS bypasses health information entirely
Every client agent is a voting server
questions.explanation: Consul DNS uses stale consistency by default. This spreads reads and can preserve discovery during quorum loss, but the returned catalog view has no hard freshness guarantee.

questions.question: A three-server Consul datacenter loses two voting servers. Which statement is correct?
options: The remaining server has quorum because it is alive
WAN gossip supplies two replacement votes
The datacenter cannot commit writes because quorum requires two voters
Client agents automatically become voters
questions.explanation: A three-voter Raft set requires a majority of two. One surviving server may answer some stale reads, but it cannot elect a leader or commit new log entries.

questions.question: What does Consul service mesh add to ordinary catalog discovery?
options: Automatic business-level retry safety
Workload identity, mTLS, proxy-mediated traffic, and intention-based authorization
A guarantee that existing denied connections are terminated immediately
Automatic database replication
questions.explanation: Consul service mesh uses workload certificates and proxies to authenticate, encrypt, and authorize service traffic. Intentions control new connections or requests; they do not make application retries idempotent.

questions.question: How should the ACL bootstrap token be handled after the initial ACL setup?
options: Install it as the default token on every client agent
Expose it to unauthenticated DNS callers
Restrict and secure it, then issue narrowly scoped agent, service, and operator tokens
Commit it beside the Consul server configuration
questions.explanation: The bootstrap token has global-management privileges. Use it only to establish policies and scoped identities, store emergency access securely, and avoid broad shared tokens.

questions.question: Consul servers are overloaded and dns_config.max_stale causes more requests to reach the leader. What is the safest response?
options: Reduce max_stale until every read is leader-served
Add more voting servers without measuring consensus latency
Remove abusive load, use eligible stale or agent-cached reads, and scale from server telemetry
Disable health checks so catalog writes stop
questions.explanation: A tight max-stale bound can turn cheap follower reads into expensive leader reads and worsen overload. Contain callers, preserve suitable local read paths, and use Raft, RPC, CPU, disk, and latency evidence before scaling.
